name: acme-journey
description: Condensed from a real live Acme session (final_tm_242431, saved verbatim under server/sessions/samples/final_tm_242431.json) that produced 0 interventions across 9 real LLM calls despite a genuine checkout bounce (checkout -> login wall -> checkout -> login -> /shop) and a cart (৳650) stuck well under the ৳1,500 free-delivery threshold while browsing /shop and product pages. Category (a)/(c) regression: state.js's patterns.checkoutBounce is deterministically true right after the bounce (verified directly against buildState(), not just via a live model call — see server/NOTES.md); the cart_under_threshold offer's fill_with gives the model a concrete one-tap fact to act on even mid-browse. Live (2026-09-12, 3 runs, LLM_CACHE=0): the model consistently acted on cart_under_threshold (target shipping-banner — its own real target_hint, legitimately visible on this store's product pages, so no anchor-fallback rewrite needed here; see sessions/nextcart-search-fix.json / templates.json's `anchor` field for a fixture that DOES exercise the fallback rewrite) but did not independently fire checkout_bounce within this compressed replay's ~2-minute window — real CLI backend latency (~11-20s/call) plus decision coalescing (max 1 in-flight + 1 pending per session) limits a replay to ~2-3 actual model calls in that time, versus the 9 the real 4-minute session got; by the time the 2nd call lands, cart_under_threshold's fresher/still-true signal wins out over the earlier bounce. This is an open prompt-tuning item (server/prompts/decide.md now explicitly tells the model to check `patterns.checkoutBounce` by name first), not a code defect — the flag itself computes correctly (see the buildState() unit check in server/NOTES.md's entry for this fix).
